key_developments.event: Traditional founding date; Irnerius teaches Roman law.
Gratian compiles the Decretum at Bologna.
Frederick I grants the Authentica Habita — imperial protection of scholars.
Honorius III's Super speculam regulates licentia docendi.

_quarry.description: The oldest continuously operating university in Europe, traditionally dated to 1088 when Irnerius began teaching Roman law from rediscovered Justinianic texts. Bologna pioneered the student-governed (rather than master-governed) model and made canon and civil law its specialty, drawing students from across Latin Europe. Gratian's Decretum (c. 1140) — the foundation of medieval canon law — was compiled there.
